top_choice_rationale: P001 (Helpman and Melitz, B038) is the most identifiable discovery with a defensible credit set. Melitz (2003) and the Helpman-Melitz-Yeaple work moved trade analysis from industries to firms. They supplied a selection and reallocation mechanism that has been tested on firm-level customs and production data for over twenty years. The exporter-premia facts came before the model, so the strongest support is for the qualitative mechanism, not for welfare magnitudes. A citation built on the mechanism avoids overclaiming. The main residual risk is attribution to Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum, which a narrow citation reduces but does not remove. Firm selection is a distinct step from the 2008 trade prize. P002 (Calvo, Taylor, Woodford) is a first-rank contribution, but the trio contests credit for the estimation phase, and the micro evidence on Calvo pricing is mixed. P003 has strong identification but bundles two strands and leaves the third name uncertain. P004 has clean attribution but thinner direct identification of the collateral channel and some overlap with the 2022 prize. I rank no award last because every proposal on the slate describes a mature and substantive contribution.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my field (labour economics, crime) is adjacent to P003, and my frequent co-authors do not appear among the credited names on any proposal
